paper.title_en: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
paper.abstract_en: Scalar-induced second-order tensor perturbations comprise both a forced response and freely propagating gravitational waves, the radiative signal sought in gravitational-wave observations. We define this free radiation as the out-state, extracted from the light-cone residue of the kernel for each scalar pair via a classical LSZ-type reduction formula. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: tensor redefinitions with power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leave the out-state invariant. For any constant equation of state $0<w<1$, the out-state is consequently universal across all intrinsic gauges, where slicing and spatial coordinates are fixed by local matter and geometry without an external clock. In this regime, the late-time Newtonian-gauge kernel yields the out-state, rigorously justifying the standard practice of computing the scalar-induced gravitational-wave energy spectrum from this kernel.
